Assuming storage always works inside sandboxed iframes.
beginnerTips: Always handle quota and privacy-mode errors with try/catch.
Prefer sessionStorage when data should die with the tab.
topics.title: localStorage overview

topics.summary: localStorage.setItem(key, value)
topics.description: setItem(key, value) writes a string under a key, replacing any previous value. Non-strings are coerced — objects become "[object Object]" unless you JSON.stringify first. Wrap writes in try/catch for quota and security errors.
topics.whenToUse: Persisting a string or stringified structure.
topics.whenNotToUse: Huge payloads that may exceed quota.
commonMistakes: setItem("user", obj) without stringify.
Swallowing exceptions and wondering why nothing saved.
beginnerTips: Namespace keys (myapp:theme) to avoid collisions.
Write after validating so you do not persist bad state.
topics.title: Storing values

topics.summary: localStorage.getItem(key) → string or null
topics.description: getItem(key) returns the stored string or null if the key is missing. Convert types yourself: JSON.parse for objects, Number for numeric strings. Provide defaults when null. Reading is synchronous — fine for small prefs, not for giant blobs on every frame.
topics.whenToUse: Restoring saved preferences or cached JSON on load.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not parse on every keystroke without need — cache in memory.
commonMistakes: JSON.parse(null) quirks — parse only when getItem returned a string.
Assuming missing keys return "" instead of null.
beginnerTips: const theme = localStorage.getItem("theme") ?? "light";
Check null before JSON.parse.
topics.title: Retrieving values

topics.summary: removeItem(key) or clear()
topics.description: removeItem(key) deletes one key. clear() wipes all keys for the origin — usually too broad for apps that share the origin with other scripts. Remove keys you no longer need so stale settings do not linger.
topics.whenToUse: Logout, reset preferences, or dropping obsolete keys.
topics.whenNotToUse: clear() on a shared origin when other features still need their keys.
commonMistakes: Calling clear() during development and wiping unrelated tools’ data on the same origin.
Typos in the key name leaving orphaned data.
beginnerTips: Version your keys (prefs:v2) and remove old versions on migrate.
Expose a “reset local data” control for users.
topics.title: Removing values

topics.summary: stringify on write, parse on read.
topics.description: Objects and arrays must be stringified before setItem and parsed after getItem. Wrap parse in try/catch in case the stored string is corrupt. A small helper pair (loadJson / saveJson) keeps call sites clean and consistent.
topics.whenToUse: Persisting structured client state.
topics.whenNotToUse: Deeply nested state that belongs on a server.
commonMistakes: Parsing without try/catch.
Saving after every tiny mutation without need — batch updates.
beginnerTips: Validate parsed data before trusting fields.
Include a version field inside the JSON for migrations.
topics.title: JSON with localStorage

topics.summary: Interfaces for talking to other systems — often over HTTP.
topics.description: An API is a defined way for programs to talk. On the web you usually call HTTP APIs that return JSON your page can display. The browser’s fetch function is the common client. APIs document URLs, methods, auth, and response shapes — read those docs before coding.
topics.whenToUse: Loading or sending data that lives outside the static page.
topics.whenNotToUse: Purely local UI state that never leaves the browser.
commonMistakes: Hard-coding secrets into front-end API calls.
Assuming the API always returns the happy-path shape.
beginnerTips: Start with a public JSON endpoint or a mock file while learning.
Treat network data as untrusted until validated.
topics.title: What APIs are

topics.summary: Methods like GET and POST, status codes, headers, body.
topics.description: HTTP requests have a method (GET to read, POST to send, etc.), URL, headers, and sometimes a body. Responses include a status code (200 ok, 404 missing, 500 server error) and a body. Understanding status codes helps you branch correctly after fetch. CORS rules can block browser calls to other origins.
topics.whenToUse: Planning how your page will load or submit data.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not use GET with a body — use POST/PUT/PATCH as appropriate.
commonMistakes: Ignoring status codes and only reading the body.
Putting sensitive data in GET query strings.
beginnerTips: Idempotent GET should not change server state.
Set Content-Type: application/json when sending JSON bodies.
topics.title: HTTP requests

topics.summary: Browser function that starts a network request and returns a Promise.
topics.description: fetch(url, options) starts a request and returns a Promise that resolves to a Response. It rejects mainly on network failure; HTTP error statuses still resolve — check response.ok or status. Read the body with response.json() or .text(). Demo fetches may fail offline; always handle errors.
topics.whenToUse: Browser HTTP calls to APIs or static JSON files.
topics.whenNotToUse: Cross-origin calls blocked by CORS without a proper server setup.
commonMistakes: Awaiting json() without checking ok.
Forgetting await and using the Promise as data.
beginnerTips: Pass { method, headers, body } in the second argument.
AbortController cancels in-flight requests when the user navigates away.
topics.title: fetch()
topics.syntax:
const res = await fetch('/data.json');
const data = await res.json();

topics.summary: Objects representing a future value: pending, fulfilled, rejected.
topics.description: A Promise represents work that finishes later. It starts pending, then fulfills with a value or rejects with an error. Chain with then/catch/finally, or use async/await. fetch, timers wrapped in promises, and many Web APIs return promises. Always handle rejection so errors are not silent.
topics.whenToUse: Any asynchronous success/failure value.
topics.whenNotToUse: Simple synchronous calculations — no need to wrap them.
commonMistakes: Floating promises with no await/catch.
Nesting then deeply instead of flattening with async/await.
beginnerTips: Return promises from functions so callers can await them.
Promise.all runs independent tasks concurrently.
topics.title: Promises

topics.summary: Syntactic sugar for writing asynchronous code that looks synchronous.
topics.description: async functions always return a Promise. Inside them you can await other promises, pausing that function until they settle. Errors from awaited promises can be caught with try/catch. Top-level await works in ES modules. Keep await in sequence only when steps depend on each other.
topics.whenToUse: Readable asynchronous flows: fetch then parse then render.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not await independent tasks one-by-one when Promise.all is faster.
commonMistakes: Using await outside async functions in classic scripts.
Wrapping everything in async without handling failures.
beginnerTips: Mark the function async before using await.
Handle errors next to the await that can fail.
topics.title: async / await

topics.summary: await response.json()
topics.description: Most APIs return JSON bodies. After fetch, call await response.json() to parse. Confirm response.ok (or status) first so you do not parse an HTML error page as JSON. Content-Type should usually include application/json, but parsing still depends on the actual body text.
topics.whenToUse: Consuming JSON APIs and local .json files.
topics.whenNotToUse: Binary downloads — use blob/arrayBuffer instead.
commonMistakes: Calling json() twice on the same response body.
Skipping ok checks and treating error payloads as success data.
beginnerTips: Clone the response if you need to read the body twice.
Show a user-friendly message when ok is false.
topics.title: JSON responses

topics.summary: Network failures reject; HTTP 404 may still resolve — check ok.
topics.description: fetch rejects when the network fails (offline, DNS, CORS failure in some cases). A 404 or 500 response still fulfills the promise — inspect response.ok or status. Use try/catch around await fetch and await response.json(). Surface useful messages to users without leaking internal details.
topics.whenToUse: Any production fetch call.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not catch errors and ignore them silently.
commonMistakes: Assuming catch handles 404 automatically.
Showing raw stack traces to end users.
beginnerTips: throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`) when !res.ok for a single catch path.
Distinguish network errors from HTTP errors in logging.
topics.title: Handling fetch errors

topics.summary: Bring exported bindings into a module.
topics.description: import pulls exported names from another module file into the current one. Use named imports { loadSection } or a default import. Module URLs are usually relative paths ending in .js. Imports are static and hoist — they run before module body code. Browsers require type="module" on the script tag.
topics.whenToUse: Sharing code across files in a front-end project.
topics.whenNotToUse: Classic non-module scripts without a bundler — import will not work.
commonMistakes: Forgetting type="module" and seeing unexpected syntax errors.
Using bare specifiers like "lodash" without an import map or bundler.
beginnerTips: Keep the .js extension in browser-native imports.
Import only what you need to keep intent clear.
topics.title: import

topics.summary: Share functions/values from a module file.
topics.description: export marks bindings other modules may import. Named exports can be many per file; default export is one “main” value. Re-export to build a public barrel file if helpful. Only export what other files need — keep the rest private to the module.
topics.whenToUse: Making helpers and components available to other files.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not export everything — a small public surface is easier to maintain.
commonMistakes: Mixing up default and named import syntax.
Circular imports that leave bindings temporally uninitialized.
beginnerTips: Prefer named exports for utilities; default for a primary class/component.
Match import names to export names for easier search.
topics.title: export
topics.syntax:
export function greet() {}
export default App;

topics.summary: Split by feature: navigation.js, search.js, etc.
topics.description: As apps grow, split code by feature or layer: ui/, api/, utils/. One entry module imports the rest and starts the app. This site’s js/ folder is an example. Keep files small enough that each has a clear job. Avoid circular dependencies by pushing shared helpers into neutral modules.
topics.whenToUse: Any project past a single script file.
topics.whenNotToUse: A tiny demo page — one file is fine until complexity appears.
commonMistakes: One 2,000-line module that everyone fears editing.
Copy-pasting the same fetch helper into five files instead of exporting it.
beginnerTips: Name files after features, not vague helpers.js dumping grounds.
Colocate related render and event code when it aids navigation.
topics.title: Organizing larger projects

topics.summary: Runtime problems that interrupt normal flow.
topics.description: Errors interrupt normal execution when something goes wrong: bad JSON, missing elements, failed network calls. The console shows a message and stack trace pointing at the call chain. Fix root causes; catch only where you can recover or show a useful message. Distinguish programmer mistakes from expected user/input failures.
topics.whenToUse: Debugging failures and designing recovery paths.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not wrap every line in try/catch — it hides bugs.
commonMistakes: Catching errors and leaving empty catch blocks.
Blaming the wrong line when the stack points at a helper.
beginnerTips: Reproduce with the smallest steps, then read the stack from the top.
Log context (ids, urls) alongside the error.
topics.title: Errors overview

topics.summary: Attempt code and handle thrown errors.
topics.description: try runs a block; if something throws, catch receives the error and runs instead of crashing the whole script. Use it around parse, fetch, and other operations that can fail for external reasons. Re-throw when you cannot handle the case so higher layers can decide.
topics.whenToUse: Recoverable failures at well-defined boundaries.
topics.whenNotToUse: Control flow for normal branches — use if instead of throw/catch.
commonMistakes: Catching everything and ignoring it.
Putting unrelated code in the same try so the catch is ambiguous.
beginnerTips: Name the error err and read err.message / err.name.
Keep try blocks small so you know what failed.
topics.title: try / catch

topics.summary: Runs after try/catch whether or not an error occurred.
topics.description: finally always runs after try (and catch if it ran), whether the try succeeded, failed, or returned early. Use it for cleanup: hiding spinners, closing resources, clearing flags. Avoid putting logic in finally that can throw and obscure the original error.
topics.whenToUse: Cleanup that must happen on both success and failure.
topics.whenNotToUse: Do not use finally for the main success logic — keep that in try.
commonMistakes: Returning from finally and overwriting a return from try.
Throwing inside finally and losing the original error.
beginnerTips: finally runs even if catch rethrows — cleanup still happens.
Prefer small, safe cleanup statements.
topics.title: finally

topics.summary: Create your own errors when invariants fail.
topics.description: throw stops the current path and sends an error to the nearest catch or up the call stack. throw new Error("message") is the usual form. Use it when a function receives invalid input or hits a state that must not continue. Include enough detail in the message to debug.
topics.whenToUse: Guard clauses and API wrappers that detect impossible or invalid states.
topics.whenNotToUse: Ordinary user mistakes you can handle with validation messages instead.
commonMistakes: Throwing plain strings instead of Error objects (weaker stacks).
Throwing for expected empty results that callers should handle as null.
beginnerTips: Custom error classes help callers distinguish failure types.
Fail fast near the source rather than returning magic nulls everywhere.
topics.title: throw
